faq.title: Get Your Questions Answered
faq.description: Everything you need to know to start your journey to the United States with legal security.

faqs.question: Who can start a legalization process in the USA?
faqs.answer: In the USA, the legalization process can be initiated by family members who are American citizens or permanent residents, by employers who sponsor work visas, by the immigrant themselves in specific cases such as asylum or extraordinary abilities, or by the government in humanitarian or refugee processes.

faqs.question: If someone entered through the border, do they have a chance to get a Green Card?
faqs.answer: Yes, someone who entered through the border has a chance to get a Green Card, but it depends on the case. Typically, entering without inspection complicates the process, but possibilities still exist, such as marrying an American citizen and requesting status adjustment through the consular process with waiver, or applying for asylum if there is real fear of persecution in the country of origin.

faqs.question: How long does an immigration process take to be approved?
faqs.answer: The time for approval of a migration process in the USA varies greatly depending on the type of petition. For example, direct family processes such as marriage to an American citizen can take 10 to 18 months, while Green Card requests for siblings can take 10 to 15 years. Asylum processes can take 2 to 5 years or more, depending on the state and queue. Work visas with labor certification typically take 1 to 3 years.

faqs.question: What types of visas do you work with?
faqs.answer: We offer specialized assistance for asylum cases, Green Card through marriage, EB-3 visas (skilled workers), E-2 (investment), SIJ (Special Immigrant Juvenile Status), and VAWA (protection for domestic violence victims). Our team also provides support for visas such as EB-1 for athletes and professionals with extraordinary abilities, F-1 (student), H-1B (specialized work), and L-1 (intra-company transfer).

faqs.question: Is there any risk when starting the process?
faqs.answer: Yes, there is risk when starting a migration process in the USA, especially if the person is out of status or entered without inspection. For example, if the request is denied, the immigrant may receive a deportation order or be placed in removal proceedings. Additionally, providing false information or incorrect documents can result in an admissibility bar (prohibition of entry) for several years or permanently. Therefore, it is essential to analyze the case with an immigration attorney before starting any process, ensuring that there is a solid legal basis and that the risks are known and calculated.

faqs.question: Is the initial consultation really free?
faqs.answer: Yes! We offer a free consultation with our consultants to evaluate your case and indicate the best path for your migration process.
